subject: psychiatry
title: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Trauma-Related Conditions

steps.tx: **Post-traumatic stress disorder** develops following direct exposure to, witnessing, or learning of actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence. Diagnosis requires symptom persistence for at least one month across four distinct symptom clusters: intrusion, avoidance, negative alterations in cognitions and mood, and autonomic hyperarousal.
steps.say: PTSD arises after exposure to severe trauma or violence, requiring at least one month of intrusive memories, avoidance, negative mood, and hyperarousal.

vis.title: PTSD Diagnostic Tetrad
rows: Reliving battlefield trauma triggered by thunder
Avoiding cars, hospitals, or discussing incident
Believing 'I am permanently ruined' or 'I am to blame'
Sitting with back to wall; explosive irritability

steps.tx: The diagnostic picture arranges post traumatic symptoms as four linked groups rather than one undifferentiated reaction to danger. Intrusion and avoidance sit opposite each other, while negative beliefs and mood form the third group and **hyperarousal** supplies the fourth, with startle, vigilance and broken sleep. Keeping the tetrad in view prevents a common error: treating nightmares alone as sufficient while missing avoidance that maintains the disorder over time.
steps.say: PTSD is organised as intrusion, avoidance, negative cognition and mood, and hyperarousal. The full tetrad must be sought, not nightmares alone.

vis.alt: Four panel PTSD symptom tetrad showing intrusion, avoidance, negative cognitions and autonomic hyperarousal
vis.caption: Intrusion, avoidance, negative cognitions and autonomic hyperarousal are drawn as the four linked clusters of PTSD. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Flashbacks and intrusive memories** represent vivid dissociative states wherein the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring in the present moment. These sensory intrusions are triggered by subtle environmental cues resembling trauma sensory features, accompanied by acute autonomic tachycardia and panic.
steps.say: Flashbacks are vivid dissociative episodes where the traumatic event feels as though it is recurring in real time, accompanied by intense terror.

left.title: Flashback Phenomenology
points: Vivid visual, auditory, or olfactory reliving
Transient loss of orientation to current reality

right.title: Standard Traumatic Recall
points: Narrative autobiographical memory of past event
Full awareness of current safe surroundings
Distressing but clearly recognized as the past

steps.tx: **Hypervigilance and exaggerated startle response** reflect persistent autonomic neurobiological sensitization and failure of medial prefrontal inhibition over an hyperactive amygdala. Patients maintain constant surveillance of their immediate surroundings, scan crowds for hidden threats, position themselves near building exits, and react explosively to unexpected sounds.
steps.say: Hypervigilance reflects continuous amygdala hyper-reactivity, causing patients to constantly scan surroundings for threats and startle at sudden noises.

right.title: Behavioral Consequences
points: Inability to sit with back to restaurant doors
Violent startle reactions to dropped objects
Chronic refractory initial and middle insomnia

steps.tx: **Acute stress reaction**, or acute stress disorder, presents with clinical features identical to PTSD but occurs immediately following trauma exposure and lasts between three days and one month. Symptoms resolving within four weeks are categorized as acute stress disorder; symptoms persisting beyond 30 days warrant formal PTSD reclassification.
steps.say: Acute stress disorder occurs within one month of trauma. If symptoms persist beyond thirty days, the diagnosis converts to post-traumatic stress disorder.

left.title: Acute Stress Disorder
points: Onset within three days of traumatic event
Duration between three days and one month
Prominent early dissociative amnesia and numbing

right.title: PTSD Classification
points: Symptoms persist beyond one full month
Can manifest with delayed onset after months
Higher risk of substance misuse and depression

steps.tx: **Adjustment disorder** is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms developing within three months of an identifiable non-life-threatening psychosocial stressor, such as divorce, business failure, or moving homes. Symptoms cause marked distress out of proportion to the stressor but resolve within six months after the stressor terminates.
steps.say: Adjustment disorder involves emotional distress out of proportion to an everyday stressor like divorce, resolving within six months of stressor cessation.

steps.tx: **Prolonged grief disorder** is diagnosed when intense yearning or longing for a deceased loved one and preoccupation with their death persists for at least 12 months in adults (or 6 months in children). Sufferers experience profound emotional pain, disbelief regarding the death, loneliness, and marked disruption in daily social functioning.
steps.say: Prolonged grief disorder involves persistent yearning and intense disbelief regarding a loved one's death lasting over twelve months in adults.

left.title: Prolonged Grief Criteria
points: Avoidance of reminders of the deceased
Inability to re-engage with personal life

right.title: Normal Bereavement
points: Waves of grief that gradually diminish
Gradual adaptation to life within a year

steps.tx: One trauma focused therapy asks the patient to hold the distressing memory in mind while tracking a moving stimulus sideways. Those alternating saccades are the visible core of **eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing**, delivered in structured phases after preparation and stabilisation. Clinicians monitor distress ratings between sets, and the method sits alongside trauma focused cognitive therapy rather than replacing assessment, safeguarding or medication review for comorbid illness.
steps.say: EMDR pairs recall of a trauma memory with bilateral eye movements in structured phases. Distress is rated between sets after preparation and stabilisation work.

vis.alt: Therapist guiding bilateral saccadic eye movements with moving fingers during an EMDR session
vis.caption: Bilateral saccadic eye movements are guided while the patient holds a trauma memory during EMDR. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Complex PTSD** incorporates the core symptoms of classical PTSD alongside severe, persistent disturbances in affect regulation, persistent beliefs of being diminished or worthless, and severe difficulties in sustaining interpersonal relationships. It characteristically results from prolonged, repeated interpersonal trauma from which escape is impossible, such as childhood abuse.
steps.say: Complex PTSD arises from chronic inescapable trauma like childhood abuse, adding severe emotional dysregulation and relational instability to standard PTSD.

vis.title: Complex PTSD Additional Triad
rows: Explosive anger, chronic suicidal ideation, dissociation
Viewing oneself as permanently broken or soiled
Alternating between emotional clinginess and hostile rejection

steps.tx: **Prazosin for trauma nightmares** operates as a centrally active alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist, dampening excessive noradrenergic transmission in the brain during rapid eye movement sleep. Clinical trials demonstrate significant reductions in trauma-related nightmares, nighttime awakenings, and sleep fragmentation, requiring bedtime titration from one to 10 milligrams.
steps.say: Prazosin blocks central alpha-1 adrenergic receptors during sleep, dramatically reducing trauma nightmares and night awakenings in PTSD.

left.title: Prazosin Nighttime Action
points: Suppresses noradrenergic surge during REM sleep
